title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed results of continuous-batching runs, concurrency targets, and queueing behavior; identified config changes and next steps to reach target 15k TPS-equivalent for short-form inference. Agreed to run extended benchmark with KV cache warm and provide trace logs. Action items assigned.
next_steps: Redwood to run a 30-minute 8-concurrency benchmark with cache warm and share CSV + graphs by 2026-03-28
NovaHealth to supply a representative 10k sample of prod prompts by 2026-03-27
Schedule latency-focused deep dive (p95/p99 tracing) next week if anomalies persist
action_items: Ravi Menon: run extended 8x concurrency throughput run with KV cache warm; upload CSV + perf graphs by 2026-03-28
Maya Chen: share 10k representative prompt set (anonymized) by 2026-03-27
Omar Ruiz: provide cluster autoscaler logs and current k8s HPA config by 2026-03-26
Alicia Park: compile pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted under projected QPS and send summary by 2026-03-29
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25 | Start: 10:30 PT | Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NovaHealth ML Eng), Omar Ruiz (NovaHealth Platform Eng), Priya Patel (NovaHealth CTO)

[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 45 mins. quick agenda — run through last week's numbers, tuning we did on continuous batching, concurrency targets, and decide next steps. sound good?
[00:12] Maya: yep, sounds good. we pulled the logs this morning, so we can walk through numbers.
[00:18] Ravi: cool, i'll start with a quick recap of what we ran. last friday we tested with the rdx-13b-quant variant, continuous batching enabled, target concurrency set to 6, and queue_max_latency at 120ms. we also tried an 8-concurrency run this morning with cache cold and warm. caveat — the sample load is synthetic but based on maya's prod-ish set.
[00:35] Maya: small note, some tokens in the test set are shorter than prod, so per-token times might be slightly optimistic.
[00:42] Ravi: noted. so results: 6 concurrency run — steady throughput ~9.2k tokens/sec, p50 latency ~80ms, p95 ~310ms, p99 ~880ms, tail due to a few long prompts. 8 concurrency warm-cache run — throughput jumped to ~12.6k tokens/sec, p50 ~95ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s. cold-cache 8x was worse as expected — big spike in p99.
[01:10] Omar: when you say tokens/sec, is that tokens emitted or tokens processed at runtime? our billing expectations are based on model tokens emitted.
[01:16] Ravi: tokens emitted, yes — same metric Redwood reports. we can also provide token-gen and compute-time CSVs.
[01:24] Priya: our SLA target is roughly equivalent to 15k tokens/sec average for short prompts during peak, and 95th percentile latency below 500ms. right now the p95 is slightly above that at 420ms for warm 8x but those long tails are concerning.
[01:38] Alicia: good callout. main levers we have: increase batching window, increase concurrency, adjust queueing/backpressure thresholds, and modify autoscaling policy to allow short bursts on Dedicated or reserved capacity. also quant profile changes (e.g., int8 vs int4) can change throughput but might affect quality.
[01:56] Maya: did you see any evidence of KV cache thrashing? our workloads have a lot of short repeated prompts so cache should help.
[02:03] Ravi: with warm-cache runs we saw cache hit rate ~73% on average; thrashing occurred when concurrency hit >10 because the KV cache eviction was triggered by the working set. there's an option to increase KV cache size per worker or pin hot prefixes for the POC.
[02:20] Omar: how does that interact with memory on the GPU? we don't want OOM issues.
[02:24] Ravi: tradeoff — larger KV cache uses more GPU DRAM; we recommended bumping GPU memory to a slightly larger instance for Dedicated or enabling prefix pinning which reduces eviction by keeping a small set of hot prefixes resident. both doable.
[02:38] Maya: any thoughts on queue_max_latency? we set 120ms, would increasing to 200ms let you batch more and improve throughput?
[02:46] Ravi: yes, increasing queue_max_latency to 200-250ms helps the runtime batch more aggressively. in our tests raising to 200ms with 8 concurrency got throughput to ~14.5k tokens/sec but p95 increased slightly to ~470ms — still within your p95 requirement of 500ms. p99 still had spikes due to a few large prompts not being priority-queued.
[03:08] Priya: those large prompts are the outliers — we can pre-classify and send them to a separate route with higher timeout. can Redwood support per-route queueing policies?
[03:18] Alicia: yes, routes and model variants can have independent queue and timeout configs; you can also set automatic fallback to a smaller model for big prompts to maintain latency SLOs.
[03:28] Omar: curious about concurrency targets — is there a recommended concurrency per GPU for rdx-13b-quant?
[03:33] Ravi: recommended starting point is 6-8 concurrent requests for short-form prompts on 80GB A10-ish hardware; if you bump to A100 or p4d style, you can push concurrency higher. our rose tests showed diminishing returns after 12 concurrency because of cache pressure and kernel saturation.
[03:49] Maya: any mis-transcriptions in logs where the runtime thought tokens were longer? we saw a few requests with massively inflated time which look like preemption.
[03:58] Ravi: we saw a few preemption events on the node where Kubernetes preempted a low-priority pod during our cold-cache run. that caused a long p99 spike. Omar, you mentioned autoscaler — do you run cluster autoscaling aggressively?
[04:10] Omar: currently HPA is set conservative; we also have a node pool that takes ~6-7 minutes to scale up which is not ideal for short bursts. we can create a buffer/reserved pool for Redwood Dedicated to reduce cold starts.
[04:22] Alicia: that fits the Dedicated/reserved pattern — for POC we can simulate reserved capacity or request a small warm pool on your side to avoid node spin-up.
[04:30] Priya: ok. what's the expected cost delta if we go to reserved versus hosted burst?
[04:34] Alicia: i'll send a short pricing delta but ballpark — reserved gives ~20-30% reduction in per-token cost at scale because of utilization and we can offer a pilot discount. i'll follow up.
[04:43] Ravi: back to tuning, we also tried increasing batching window from 16ms to 40ms. throughput improved by ~22% but p50 rose by ~12ms. that tradeoff looked acceptable for your SLAs.
[04:57] Maya: did that increase jitter on tail?
[05:00] Ravi: slightly. the tail moved a bit because some requests waited longer to form a batch, but the p95 remained similar. again, per-route tuning solves that.
[05:09] Alicia: action items recap coming up, but any other blockers?
[05:13] Maya: one more — we need trace-level p99 breakdowns, not just latency percentiles, to see where time is spent (scheduling vs decode vs kernel). can you provide traces?
[05:20] Ravi: yes, we can dump per-request traces and a flamegraph; we'll sanitize traces to remove any PII.
[05:26] Omar: and we'll send current HPA logs and the k8s autoscaler config.
[05:30] Priya: timeline—if we get the 10k prompt set out monday, can we expect these numbers to be validated by wednesday?
[05:37] Ravi: yes, if we get the prompt set by friday morning ideally we can run extended 30-minute benchmarks over the weekend and share results monday/tuesday. but we'll aim for the deadlines we set in action items.
[05:47] Alicia: great. quick recap: 1) Ravi to run extended 8x concurrency warm-cache run and share CSV + perf graphs by 2026-03-28. 2) Maya to share anonymized 10k prompt set by 2026-03-27. 3) Omar to share autoscaler logs and HPA by 2026-03-26. 4) Alicia to send Dedicated vs Hosted pricing summary by 2026-03-29. 5) Plan a p95/p99 trace deep-dive next week if tail persists.
[06:10] Maya: thanks, that works.
[06:12] Priya: thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
Notes: occasional transcription errors present; speaker turns sometimes missing punctuation. Shared artifacts: link to perf CSV (internal), perf dashboard screenshot (screenshot link), POC prompt set (to be shared).
